overall: Board violated the OML by failing to post its December 4 meeting notice at the official location (clerk's office building), since the town never notified the AG of adopting its website. The 40A claim was declined; no further remedy was needed because the town has since filed notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to post notice for its December 4 meeting in compliance with the Open Meeting Law, as notice was only on the town website.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board failed to post notice to the Town’s official notice posting location, which at the time was in or on the municipal building in which the clerk’s office is located.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to comply with the notice requirements of G.L. c. 40A, § 11 for the December 4 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review Mr. Calhoun’s second complaint.

allegations.summary: Later correspondence raised concern that the town had not posted the required notice telling the public where to find meeting notices online.
allegations.key_passage: Because this allegation was not raised in either complaint, we do not make a finding regarding whether the Town has complied with the regulation.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
